title: The Burning Oath Revisited
premise: For two hundred years the valley of Crane's Hollow has been sealed by wards that keep magic out — and its last swordspeaker, Ada Crane, in. When the border wards collapse on the night every star vanishes from the sky, Ada is dragged through the breach by a dying dragon's ember and into a realm where oaths are literal chains. He discovers his family's covenant with the dragon-clans was not kept but betrayed, and that the extinguished stars are the souls of dragons whose fire-forges have gone dark. Hunted by the Warden who once loved his mother, and bound to a disgraced oath-keeper named Sef who knows the truth of the betrayal, Ada must choose between restoring his family's honor and speaking the truth that will shatter it. In the end, Ada reforges the covenant not with an inherited lie but with a new oath spoken in his own voice — reigniting the last dragon-fire at the cost of the valley's isolation, and returning home changed, with the stars burning overhead.
about_author: Yara Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken treaties before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about the weight of inherited promises from a farmhouse full of rescued animals.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. On the eve of his oath-binding ceremony, Ada tends the valley's cold hearth and feels the wards hum wrong. At midnight, every star vanishes and the border stones crack like ice. The chapter ends with something enormous falling through the breach toward him. Emotional beat: dread beneath the comfort of a life about to be chosen for him.

chapters.title: Ember in the Ashfall
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. A dying dragon's ember crashes into the valley square, dragging Ada through the collapsing ward into the outer realm. He wakes among ash fields under a starless sky, the ember fused to his palm — the mark of a swordspeaker's bond he never swore. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant wonder as the world he was taught to fear becomes real.

chapters.title: The Warden's Road
chapters.summary: POV: Ada, with interludes from Warden Ilse Vane. Ilse, who loved Ada's mother, hunts him across the ashlands, believing he stole the ember. Ada is captured by Sef, a disgraced oath-keeper who recognizes the mark and claims the Cranes' covenant was broken from the inside. Emotional beat: the first crack in everything Ada believed about his family.

chapters.title: What the Covenant Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. Sef leads Ada to a ruined forge-shrine and shows him the original covenant stone: the Cranes didn't seal magic out of the valley to protect it — they sealed witnesses in. The last dragon-fire is guttering because the oath that fed it was fed on a lie. Emotional beat: grief curdling into anger as inheritance reveals itself as theft.

chapters.title: Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Seeking allies, they reach the cinder-court of the dragon-clans, where remnant dragons debate surrendering to extinction rather than serve oath-breakers. Ada is tested with his mother's old oaths and fails them all — until he speaks one truth aloud that no Crane ever dared. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into the first taste of self-authorship.

chapters.title: Ilse's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse Vane. Ilse corners Ada and offers him passage home if he surrenders the ember; she believes restoring the wards will save what remains of both realms. She reveals she helped conceal the betrayal decades ago to protect Ada's mother. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as love wearing duty's armor — and Ada refusing her anyway.

chapters.title: The Guttering Forge
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. They race to the Last Forge beneath the dead stars and find it nearly dark, guarded by the hollowed echo of the first Crane, who still enforces the ancestral oath. Sef sacrifices their freedom to buy Ada an hour at the anvil. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve as time burns down.

chapters.title: Anvil of Voices
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. To reforge the covenant, Ada must speak a new oath — but the echo of his ancestor and Ilse's arriving wardens demand he repeat the old lie. In the climax, Ada speaks the whole truth of the betrayal into the forge, letting it burn away his family name, and hammers the ember into a new covenant stone. Emotional beat: the cost of truth paid willingly.

chapters.title: Starfire
chapters.summary: POV: Ada and Sef. The forge ignites; the extinguished stars relight one by one as freed dragon-souls return to the sky. Ilse, unmade by the truth she defended, chooses at last to stand with Ada against the collapsing wards. Emotional beat: catharsis — fire as forgiveness rather than punishment.

chapters.title: The Open Valley
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Ada returns to Crane's Hollow, now open to the sky and the world, and plants the new covenant stone where the border stood. The valley mourns its isolation and begins to heal; Sef stays, and something like love takes root. Final image: Ada teaching the first children born under stars to speak oaths of their own. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
